Treat environment-specific values (backend base URLs, account endpoints, feature flags) as configuration that must be resolved from a single, centralized source rather than hardcoded or duplicated across components. Build all environment-dependent links or behaviors through one shared resolver/builder so every UI element (dashboard, usage, billing, privacy links, etc.) consistently respects the configured environment (production, proxy, self-hosted), instead of mixing hardcoded constants with resolved values.

Fetch such configuration once during app/session startup and cache it for the lifetime of the app; only retry the lookup on failure (e.g., reconnect after an unanswered startup query). Avoid re-fetching or re-resolving on every refresh or state change when the underlying environment is not expected to change at runtime.

Keep configuration-driven UI affordances in one place: don't duplicate the same setting/link across unrelated sections (e.g., don't add an account privacy link under a general "Telemetry" section when it already lives in the Account view), since this creates redundant dependencies and inconsistent behavior.

Finally, feature flags and cached config should only gate visibility/availability of a feature in the UI—they are not authorization. Perform the actual validation (connectivity, permissions, dirty state, remote checks, etc.) against live state at the time the action executes, rather than trusting a cached snapshot as proof of eligibility.

Example:
```ts
// Bad: hardcoded + duplicated across call sites
const dashboardUrl = "https://app.cline.bot/dashboard";
const usageUrl = "https://app.cline.bot/usage"; // always production

// Good: single builder resolves once-cached base URL
const { clineAppBaseUrl } = useAccount(); // resolved once at startup, cached
const buildAccountUrl = (path: string) =>
  clineAppBaseUrl ? `${clineAppBaseUrl}/${path}` : undefined;

const dashboardUrl = buildAccountUrl("dashboard");
const usageUrl = buildAccountUrl("usage");
```</description>
